document.title: The Secretary's Lunch With Pakistani Foreign Minister Abdul Sattar (State 109130)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] Secretary Powell lunches with Foreign Minister Sattar on June 19, 2001 to discuss Afghanistan, U.S. sanctions and Pakistan-China relations. Powell asks Pakistan to explain its involvement in Afghanistan, noting differing U.S. and Pakistani perspectives on the Taliban. Sattar calls the Pakistan-Taliban relationship "reasonable, but not problem free" and lists smuggling, refugee flows and Pakistani fugitives as points of contention.

events.description: Secretary's lunch with Pakistani FM Abdul Sattar; discussion of Taliban, sanctions, engagement vs. isolation.
Secretary Powell hosted lunch for Pakistani FM Sattar and delegation discussing Taliban, sanctions and China.
Powell said sanctions on Pakistan were under review and urged progress, citing IMET prohibition.
Sattar, Aziz Khan and Jilani urged engagement with the Taliban rather than isolation.

key_claims: Pakistani officials urged US engagement with the Taliban rather than isolation.
Pakistani officials portrayed Taliban leaders as young, uneducated men who would moderate with exposure to the outside world.
Sattar claimed the GOP had only limited influence with the Taliban, which listens but acts in its own interests.
Pakistan listed refugee/migrant flows, smuggling and fugitives as problems in relations with the Taliban.
The Secretary said sanctions on Pakistan were under review and asked Pakistan to show progress on US concerns.
